hypothesis: Affine Q3 gate/up with Q4 down can reduce expert storage by at least 14% without more than 3% operator latency cost.
expected_effect: Establish a bounded storage/kernel feasibility result before original-weight conversion or coding-quality evaluation.
controlled_change: Eight real expert records across layers 0/16/32/47, teacher-forced input fixtures, group-64 Q3 with BF16 metadata, unchanged Q4 down; rows 1/2/4/8, five alternating timing pairs.
correctness: All 32 real-weight operator cases passed exact expanded-code arithmetic checks with separate Metal validation. No original-weight or model-quality claim.
outcome: Padded records shrink from 2768896 to 2359296 bytes (14.79%). One-token geometric latency ratio is 1.05798, 95% interval 0.92736-1.20700. The latency gate is inconclusive, not a proven regression. Held-out capture was not run.
smallest_experiment: Only consider a preregistered operator-only timing protocol on preserved fixtures to resolve variance; do not begin full conversion or quality qualification from this result.
limitations: Single M1 Pro host; short screens cannot qualify 2K/4K generation or sustained coding.
